title: FA/69/2017 of Smt Suman Verma Vs Somprakash Verma

paras.text:
Reserved Judgment
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
First Appeal No. 69 of 2017
Smt. Suman Verma ................ Appellant

versus
Somprakash Verma ................ Respondent
Mr. M.S. Tyagi, learned counsel for the appellant.
Mr. Rajat Mittal, learned counsel for the respondent.
Coram : Hon'ble Sudhanshu Dhulia, J.
Hon'ble Lok Pal Singh, J.

[Per: Hon. Lok Pal Singh, J.]
 Present first appeal has been directed against
the judgment and decree dated 17.05.2014, passed by the
learned Principal Judge, Family Court, Dehradun, in
Matrimonial Suit No. 07 of 2014, Somprakash Verma vs
Smt. Suman Verma, whereby the divorce petition filed by
the respondent-husband, under Section 13 of the Hindu
Marriage Act, 1955, had been allowed ex parte and
marriage between the parties is dissolved. The appellant is
also aggrieved against dismissal of her application 3-A
(Order 9 rule 13 read with Section 151 CPC) for setting
aside the ex parte judgment dated 17.05.2014, which was
dismissed, vide order dated 30.05.2017, passed by Principal
Judge, Family Court, Dehradun, in Misc. case no. 28 of
2014, Smt. Suman Verma vs Somprakash Verma.

2
2) Heard learned counsel for the parties and
perused the lower court record.
3) Brief facts of the case are that the appellant and
the respondent were married on 28.04.2003, as per Hindu
rites and rituals at Dehradun. A daughter and a son were
born out of said wedlock on 13.09.2004 and 17.05.2006,
respectively. The respondent-husband has said in the
divorce petition filed before the court below that soon after
the marriage, the behaviour of the appellant-wife has
become very offensive and disrespectful. She started
behaving with respondent-husband in a cruel manner. On
respondent-husband's trying to persuade her, appellant-wife used to commit maar peet with here in-laws and treat
him and his parents with disrespect. Appellant-wife
repeatedly kept on saying that my marriage with you has
been solemnized forcibly, whereas she could marry a rich
person of her choice. On this, respondent-husband tried his
best to make the appellant-wife understand that now all
these things have no relevance as their marriage had
already been solemnized. After the birth of the children,
the appellant-wife tried to avoid the company of her
husband. In this way she did not consummate the marriage.
Gradually, the behaviour of the appellant-wife became
more violent and cruel towards her husband. It is further
pleaded in the divorce petition that appellant-wife used to
keep the keys of the steel almirah of the respondent-husband under her control, in which jewellery and
important documents were kept. On 12.06.2013, when the
mother of the respondent-husband asked for the keys for

3
taking out her gold chain from the almirah, appellant-wife
told that the keys were lost and left her matrimonial house
without informing the respondent-husband and his family
members. She could be traced only after a long search.
When the almirah was opened, it was found that the keys of
jewellery box kept inside the almirah were also missing.
When the lock of the box was broken, the valuable
jewellery and documents were found missing. On being
asked, the appellant-wife talked over mobile to one Fahim
Ahamad @ Shibbu and it was revealed that she had given
the jewellery and Rs.70,000/- to Fahim Ahamad. After said
incident, the respondent-husband dropped the appellant-wife to her parental house on 12.06.2013 and since then,
she is residing there. Respondent-husband tried to
persuade the appellant-wife to come back to her
matrimonial house, but she straight away refused to do so
and was living separately since last six months on her own
free will. Due to such cruel behaviour of the appellant-wife, the father of the respondent-husband passed away in a
state of shock. With these averments, petition under
Section 13 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, was moved by
the husband before the Principal Judge, Family Court,
Dehradun.
4) The divorce petition was filed on 04.01.2014,
i.e. on Saturday. This Court cannot lose sight of the fact
that the Advocates refrains working on Saturdays in
Dehradun. From the perusal of record, it would reveal that
initially the year was mentioned as '2013' in the order
sheet, but after correction it was mentioned as '2014'. The

4
order sheet recorded at the time of institution of the suit is
being extracted here-in-below:
04-01-2014 Present petition is filed today by the
plaintiff under Section 13 of the Hindu
Marriage Act, it was ordered that -
Register the case. Summons be issued
against the opposite party for
mediation and compromise fixing
05.03.2014.

Principal Judge
Application 5C-2 for seeking permission to appoint
Advocate was presented and it is ordered -
 Principal Judge
5) It would depict from the order sheet dated
04.01.2014 that at the time of fixing the date while issuing
summons against the opposite party for mediation and
compromise, there is an overwriting.
6) The order sheet dated 05.03.2014, is also
reproduced here-in-below:
05.03.14 File put up. Case called out.
Petitioner is present, opposite party is
not present. There is sufficient service
upon the opposite party, which is
apparent from AD 9A-2 is received
back.
In the absence of opposite party,
the case is being proceeded ex parte.
List the case on 05.05.2014 for
recording ex parte evidence of the
petitioner.
 s/d
Principal Judge

7) From the perusal of order sheet dated
04.01.2014, it would reveal that the petitioner was not

5
directed to take steps for service upon the opposite party. It
would further reveal from the order sheet as well as from
the record that there was no postal receipt of sending the
summons to the opposite party (appellant herein) through
Registered Post.
8) From the perusal of paper no. 9A-2, the alleged
A.D., it would reveal that it does not bear the signatures of
appellant. The registered A.D. was received back showing
- 'delivered to Indrajeet' on 11.01.2014. Neither the postal
receipt, nor the copy of summons is available on record.
When summons are issued through registered post, a copy
of the notice / summons is always kept on the record so that
it may prove for which date the summons were issued
through registered post. This is not the case here.
9) The procedure for issue and service of
summons has been prescribed in Order V Rule 1 of the
Code of Civil Procedure, 1908. The relevant part of Order
V Rule 1 CPC says that when a suit has been duly
instituted, a summons may be issued to the defendant to
appear and answer the claim and to file the written
statement of his defence, if any, within thirty days from the
date of serviced of summons on that defendant. Order V
Rule 1 is excerpted here-in-below for convenience:
"1. Summons . -(1) When a suit has been duly
instituted, a summons may be issued to the
defendant to appear and answer the claim and to
file the written statement of his defence, if any,
within thirty days from the date of service of
summons on that defendant.

6
Provided that no such summons shall be
issued when a defendant has appeared at the
presentation of plaint and admitted the plaintiff's
claim:
Provided further that where the defendant
fails to file the written statement within the said
period of thirty days, he shall be allowed to file the
same on such other day as may be specified by the
Court, for reasons to be recoded in writing, but
which shall not be later than ninety days from the
date of service of summons.
(2) A defendant to whom a summons has
been issued under sub-rule (1) may appear -
(a) in person, or
(b) by a pleader duly instructed and
able to answer all material questions
relating to the suit, or
(c) by a pleader accompanied by some
person able to answer all such
questions.
 (3) Every such summons shall be signed
by the Judge or such officer as he appoints, and shall
be sealed with the seal of the Court."
10) From the perusal of order sheet dated
04.01.2014, it would reveal that as per mandate of Rule 1
or Order V, no summons have been issued to the defendant
to appear and answer the claim and to file the written
statement of her defence. Rather, it is apparent from the
order sheet that the notices were issued for mediation and
compromise and not for filing the written statement and to
contest the suit. Thus, there is no compliance of Rule 1 of
Order V CPC in issuing of summons to the defendant
(appellant herein).

7
11) Order V Rule 5 of the Code of Civil Procedure
prescribed the procedure for 'summons to be either to settle
issues or for final disposal', but in the present case, there is
no compliance either of Rule 1 or Rule 5 of Order V of
Code of Civil Procedure. Sub-Rule (3) of Rule 9 of Order
V of Code of Civil Procedure provides that the service of
summons shall be made at the expenses of the plaintiff, but
from the perusal of the order sheet, it would reveal that
there is no direction for service of summons on the
defendant at the expenses of the plaintiff. Thus, again there
is no compliance of Sub-Rule (3) of Rule 9 of Order V
CPC. From the perusal of order sheet dated 04.01.2014, it
would further reveal that the summons were issued for
mediation and compromise fixing 05.03.2014, and not for
filing the written statement and appearance of the
defendant. But, without taking notice of the order dated
04.01.2014, the Principal Judge, Family Court, Dehradun
proceeded ex parte against the defendant (appellant herein)
presuming that the summons were issued to the defendant
for filing the written statement and to contest the suit.
Thus, the court below has apparently committed illegality
in not adopting the procedure prescribed for effecting
service on the defendant. The Principal Judge, Family
Court has also not recorded his satisfaction that any
summons were served through registered post upon the
defendant. From the perusal of acknowledgement (A.D.), it
would reveal that the same bears the signatures of Indrajeet,
but who is Indrajeet is nowhere mentioned in the order
sheet and how the court below has arrived to the conclusion
that the defendant has been served sufficiently. Since, the

8
Principal Judge, Family Court has not recorded his
satisfaction that the defendant has been served personally,
there was no occasion for him to proceed ex parte against
the defendant as was done by him vide order dated
05.03.2014 and subsequently after recording the ex parte
evidence of the plaintiff to decide the divorce petition by ex
parte judgment and decree dated 17.05.2014.
12) This Court is of the view that there is a flagrant
violation of the provisions laid down under Order V of the
CPC while effecting the alleged service upon the defendant
(appellant herein). It is settle proposition of law that where
a statute provides that a particular act is to be done in a
particular manner, it must be done in that manner alone.
The Principal Judge, Family Court did not comply with this
settled proposition of law by issuing the alleged summons
to the defendant (appellant herein) and proceeding ex parte
against the defendant and finally deciding the suit ex parte.
13) From the perusal of order sheet, it would
further reveal that the plaintiff (respondent herein), who
filed the divorce petition, succeeded in obtaining the ex
parte judgment and decree of divorce dated 17.05.2014
against the defendant (appellant herein), on contrary pleas
taken by him in the divorce petition.
14) On an application filed by the appellant-wife
for setting aside the ex parte judgment and decree dated
17.05.2014, on the ground of non-service of summons upon
her, though the application for setting aside the decree has

9
not been drafted properly, but this Court cannot lose sight
of the fact that the Principle Judge, Family Court has
proceeded with the case in flagrant violation of law and
committed illegality in firstly issuing notice and in
recording the service sufficient upon the defendant without
there being any evidence for the same on record. This
Court also cannot lose sight to the fact that on contrary
pleas and without there being any evidence led by the
plaintiff, decree of divorce was passed ex parte against the
defendant and the marriage between the parties was
dissolved. While deciding the application filed under
Order 9 Rule 13 CPC read with Section 151 CPC, the
learned court below has committed patent illegality in
holding that the service was effected upon the father of the
defendant (appellant herein) whereas there is no whisper in
its order dated 05.03.2014 that the service has been effected
on the father of the defendant. It is settled proposition of
law that every matter should be decided on merits and not
on technical grounds, but again the Principal Judge, Family
Court, Dehradun failed in appreciating this settled
proposition of law and committed illegality in dismissing
the said application.
15) Admittedly at the time of institution of divorce
petition the appellant-wife was residing at her parental
house with her father. It would reveal from the perusal of
lower court record that summons were not served upon the
appellant personally, rather it has come on record that
summons allegedly were served upon one Indrajeet.

10
16) The learned court below observed in its
judgment that service is sufficient on the opposite party. It
further observed that the opposite party is neither present in
the court, nor any written statement has been filed by her,
as such the matrimonial suit is being proceeded ex parte
against her.
17) The court below after perusing the affidavit
paper no. 10A filed by the husband (respondent herein),
reiterating almost the same averments as mentioned in the
divorce petition, found that the averments made by the
husband were duly supported by his ex parte evidence and
there was no rebuttal of the same on the record on behalf of
the opposite party and in absence of any other evidence, the
suit of the husband for dissolution of marriage is liable to
be decreed ex parte. The court below, accordingly, decreed
the suit filed by the husband under Section 13 of the Hindu
Marriage Act, 1955, ex parte, against the opposite party
with costs. The marriage dated 28.04.2003 between the
parties is dissolved by the decree of divorce. Aggrieved
against the judgments and decree passed by the court
below, the opposite party (wife) moved an application 3-A
for restoration of the suit and for setting aside the ex parte
judgment dated 17.05.2014. Said application was also
dismissed by the Principal Judge, Family Court, Dehradun,
vide order dated 30.05.2017, in misc. case no. 28 of 2014.
Hence, present appeal was filed by the appellant (wife).
18) Admittedly, respondent Som Prakash Verma
got married to appellant Suman Verma on 28.04.2003. It is

11
also not disputed that two children were born out of said
wedlock. From the evidence on record it is also clear that
the parties are living separately since June 2013.
19) It is an admitted fact that the decree of
divorce was passed against the appellant-wife ex parte,
without hearing her. Learned court below in its order
dated 17.05.2014, observed that opposite party has been
served sufficiently.

20) Proceedings of the matrimonial suit
proceeded ex parte against the wife and the judgment
was delivered on 17.05.2014, after affidavit was filed
on behalf of the husband. Thereafter, restoration
application filed by the appellant-wife for setting aside
the ex parte judgment was also dismissed by the court
below on 30.05.2017.

21) It is stated in para 6 of the grounds taken in
the appeal that matrimonial suit was instituted on
04.01.2014 and the suit was decreed ex parte on
17.05.2014, within a period of four months by deeming
the service sufficient upon the appellant and no effort
has been made to make the service effective upon the
appellant, which shows the conduct of the respondent in
obtaining the ex parte decree against the appellant. In
para 8 of the grounds, it has been stated that the
respondent failed to prove his case before the learned
court below by producing the independent witnesses

12
and the orders impugned are based on perverse finding
and therefore are liable to be set aside. In para 9 of the
grounds, a plea has been taken that the appellant is an
illiterate women and put her thumb impression on the
documents where it is necessary and is unable to
understand the contents of any documents, unless the
same are explained to her. The respondent took the
benefit of her illiteracy and now wants to get rid of the
appellant. It is contended that contrary findings have
been recorded against the appellant and, therefore,
impugned judgment and decree is liable to be set aside.
22) It is pertinent to mention here the principle of
law laid down by Hon'ble Apex Court in G.P. Srivastava
vs R.K. Raizada and others, (2003) 3 SCC 54. Para 7 of
said judgment reads as under:
"Under Order 9 Rule 13 of Code of Civil
Procedure, an ex parte decree passed against a defendant
can be set aside upon satisfaction of the Court that either
the summons were not duly served upon the defendant or
he was prevented by any "sufficient cause" from
appearing when the suit was called on for hearing.
Unless "sufficient cause" is shown for non-appearance of
the defendant in the case on the date of hearing, the Court
has no power to set aside an ex parte decree. The words
"was prevented by any sufficient cause from appearing"
must be liberally construed to enable the court to do
complete justice between the parties particularly when no
negligence or inaction is imputable to the erring party.
Sufficient cause for the purpose of Order 9 Rule 13 has to
be construed as an elastic expression for which no hard

13
and fast guidelines can be prescribed. The courts have a
wide discretion in deciding the sufficient cause keeping
in view the peculiar facts and circumstances of each case.
The "sufficient cause" for non-appearance refers to the
date on which the absence was made a ground for
proceeding ex parte and cannot be stretched to rely upon
other circumstances anterior in time. If "sufficient
cause" is made out for non-appearance of the defendant
on the date fixed for hearing when ex parte proceedings
were initiated against him, he cannot be penalized for his
previous negligence which had been overlooked and
thereby condoned earlier. In a case where the defendant
approaches the court immediately and within the
statutory time specified, the discretion is normally
exercised in his favour, provided the absence was not
mala fide or intentional. For the absence of a party in the
case the other side can be compensated by adequate costs
and the lis decided on merits."
23) For the just and proper adjudication of present
appeal, following moot questions are required to be
answered in this appeal:
(i) As to whether the learned Principal Judge, Family
Court has passed the decree of divorce without
proving the grounds of cruelty in favour of the
husband by way of passing an ex parte judgment and
decree dated 17.05.2014, or not?
(ii) As to whether the Principal Judge, Family Court was
right in proceeding ex parte against the wife without
their being any sufficient service upon her in
contravention of the provisions contained in Rule 1,

14
Rule 3 and Rule 9 of Order V of Code of civil
Procedure?
24) The obvious reply to question no. (i) is that
there were contrary pleadings in the divorce petition,
firstly, the husband has levelled allegations against the wife
in regard to the cruelty and maar peet with her in-laws and
stealing of ornaments and documents from the almirah and
on said allegations, respondent-husband left the appellant-wife to her parental house. Secondly, respondent-husband
stated that the appellant-wife did not return back despite his
repeated insistence for the same. Despite the contrary facts
and without their being any proof of cruelty, as pleaded by
the husband, there was no occasion for learned Principal
Judge, Family Court to pass a decree of divorce as marriage
between Hindus is not a contract, rather it is sacrosanct,
unless a party who is alleging cruelty against the opposite
party has proved the allegations of cruelty, whether
physical or mental is not entitled for decree of divorce.
But, in the present case, neither physical / mental cruelty
was pleaded nor proved by any evidence. Rather, contrary
pleadings have been taken that the wife did not come back
to the matrimonial house and left the company of husband
without sufficient cause. If it was a case of the husband
that the wife committed cruelty with him and her in-laws,
the decree of divorce could be passed only when the wife
deliberately is not joining the company of the husband for
more than two years on the ground of desertion, but the
learned Principal Judge, Family Court had passed the
decree without proving any fact of cruelty and without

15
application of mind and ignoring the provisions contained
in Section 13 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955.
25) The answer to question no. (ii) is that since
there was no service upon the wife and the learned
Principal Judge, Family Court in a whimsical manner
proceeded to decide the case ex parte without recording his
satisfaction regarding service upon the appellant-wife. The
Principal Judge, Family Court has also erred in law in not
considering the fact that the alleged summons were not
issued to the wife to contest the case by filing her written
statement and simply disposed of the case. The Principal
Judge, Family Court ought not have passed the decree of
divorce ex parte against the defendant-wife without
affording opportunity to her to contest the case by filing the
written statement.
26) The view of this Court is fortified by the view
taken by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a recent judgment in
the case of Auto Cars vs Trimurti Cargo Movers Pvt.
Ltd. and others [Civil Appeal no. 2113 of 2018 decided
on 15.02.2018], wherein it has been observed as under:
"27. The object behind sending the summons
is essentially threefold -First, it is to apprise the
defendant about the filing of a case by the plaintiff
against him; Second, to serve the defendant with the
copy of the plaint filed against him; and Third, to
inform the defendant about actual day, date, year,
time and particular Court so that he is able to appear
in the Court on the date fixed for his / her appearance
in the said case and answer the suit either personally
or through his lawyer."
27) Thus, in the light of foregoing discussion, this
Court is of the considered opinion, that the learned

16
Principal Judge, Family Court has committed gross
illegality in proceeding ex party against the appellant-wife.
In the above facts and circumstances, the impugned
judgment and decree dated 17.05.2014 as well as order
dated 30.05.2017 for restoration of matrimonial suit, cannot
sustain in the eyes of law. The impugned judgment and
decree, as also the order dated 30.05.2017, are hereby set
aside. The appeal is allowed. The matter is remanded back
to the Principal Judge, Family Court, Dehradun to decide
the divorce petition afresh, in accordance with law, after
giving opportunity of hearing to the appellant-wife to file
her written statement. Since the suit pertains to the year
2014, it is hoped and expected that the court below shall
explore all possibilities to decide the divorce petition
expeditiously and unnecessary adjournments to either of
the parties should be avoided. Lower Court records be also
sent back.

(Lok Pal Singh, J.) (Sudhanshu Dhulia, J.)
Dt. May 03, 2018. Negi
